title: Between this, Tammy Faye and Teeth- religious trauma is IN right now!...
transcript: The cast for the show is absolutely insane. We got Shailene Woodley, Zachary Quinto, Barbie Ferreira. We got Roberta Colindres of Fun Home fame. So I was obviously very excited to see this show. But the question is, does the play live up to the cast? And I'm happy to say that, yes, it does. I loved this play. Now, this is very much a play about religious trauma. So if you are someone that has religious trauma in your family, this play may hit hard. It is about four adult siblings who all grew up in a very religious household coming back home for the holidays. Don't wanna give away too much of the plot beyond that because I think that this is one of those plays that is better to just go in blind. I will say that I found this to be a fascinating meditation on family and religion and love and specifically the way that love can be weaponized by those who are super religious. I do think that the ambiguity of the show is not going to be for everyone. This is not really a show that gives you a lot of answers or gives you a clear message to take away. It instead is more interested in just presenting a ton of viewpoints and letting you, the audience, decide for yourselves. And I think it leaves a lot of debate to be add around. A lot of these characters and decisions that they Make and if it was a good decision or a bad decision. And personally, I love plays that leave you with a lot to dissect and talk about. I also was taken aback by how realistic a lot of the dialogue in the show is. Like, so many lines where I was like, oh, I know someone who talks exactly like that. I'm happy to say that all of the performances are really great, including Shailene Woodley and Barbie Ferreira, who are both making their Broadway debuts. I have been a long time fan of Zachary Quinto and wanted to see him live for forever, so I was so excited to see him in this. But honestly, the entire cast is so good, and they feel like a real family, too, which I think is so cool. So if you like well acted family dramas or plays that explore religious trauma, this play is definitely for you.
reasoning: The reviewer expresses strong enthusiasm with 'I loved this play' and gives a clear recommendation 'this play is definitely for you.' They praise multiple aspects including cast, performances, dialogue, and thematic depth.
